title: Flare Knockout Drum
model_title: Flare Knockout Drum (Horizontal, Split Entry) with Pump-Out Pumps & Heating Coil

introduction.definition: A flare knockout drum removes liquid from relief gas before the flare. The large horizontal drum (split entry, central outlet) slows the gas so droplets settle; liquid is held and pumped out. This prevents a burning liquid rain from the flare tip.
applications: Main flare systems of refineries and gas plants
Unit flare headers with liquid carry-over
key_points: Hold-up ≈ 20–30 min of largest liquid release
introduction.summary: A flare knockout drum removes liquid from relief gas before it reaches the flare, so burning liquid cannot rain down. The large horizontal drum slows the gas so droplets settle, and pump-out pumps remove the liquid.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Droplet settling velocity vs size (drag correlation).

pressure.title: Slow the gas so liquid drops out
pressure.description: Relief streams often carry liquid; a burning liquid rain from the flare is dangerous. The KO drum is sized (API 521 method) so the vapour velocity is low enough for droplets of ≈ 300–600 µm to settle in the travel time between inlet and outlet, and with hold-up volume for the liquid from the largest relief case for ≈ 20–30 min. It operates near atmospheric pressure, so pressure drop is kept small; pump-out pumps empty it.

video_tutorials.title: Flare Knockout Drum — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Flare Knockout Drum.
A flare knockout drum removes liquid from relief gas before the flare.
The large horizontal drum (split entry, central outlet) slows the gas so droplets settle; liquid is held and pumped out.
This prevents a burning liquid rain from the flare tip.
Typical applications include main flare systems of refineries and gas plants; unit flare headers with liquid carry-over.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Pump-Out Pump 1 (duty, auto on level), Pump-Out Pump 1 (duty, auto on level) — Shaft & Coupling (turning), Pump-Out Pump 2 (standby, auto on level), Pump-Out Pump 2 (standby, auto on level) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Flare Knockout Drum works.
Relief gas enters at both ends.
Gas slows across the drum.
Droplets settle out.
Pumps remove the liquid on level.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Relief streams often carry liquid; a burning liquid rain from the flare is dangerous.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flare Knockout Drum.
Check level and pump status.
Test high-level alarm.
Internal inspection.
Watch for liquid carry-over to flare: burning rain, smoke. Common cause: high level.
Watch for frozen drain: no pump-out. Common cause: coil failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
